Review content: I've read a number of reviews here and I'm left wondering if some of these people went to the same hospital I visited.2 1/2 months ago I had total knee replacement surgery performed by Dr. Goh Eng Tet. I am a citizen of the USA and I can honestly say the care I received at Loh Guan Lye was the best I have ever received. Dr. Goh exudes confidence and capability. I felt fortunate to have found him and have him perform the surgery.I was so impressed by the cleanliness and efficiency of the hospital. The same morning I had my initial consultation with Dr. Goh I was immediately scheduled for all the pre-surgery tests. X-rays, ECG, blood test and ultrasound were all performed in approximately 2 hours and results were ready for review the same day. This is unheard of in the USA. This process alone takes weeks or months to complete. I met with Dr. Goh the following day as I needed an additional test as a result of the previous day tests. When that was completed we reviewed all the tests results and I was cleared for surgery. He said he could perform the surgery on Friday, 5 days after the initial consultation. In the US this process would take 6 months to finally be scheduled for surgery. Du to my own situation, I needed to delay until the following Monday.Everything about my experience with Loh Guan Lye exceeded my expectations. Of the many things that impressed me with the hospital and the skill of Dr. Goh were the staff at the hospital. Every person I encountered was friendly, helpful and professional. From Dr Goh and his assistant, the receptionists, the lab technicians, the nurses who cared for me after surgery, my physical therapist and even those who served my meals and cleaned my hospital room, they all seemed to share one common characteristic. They all seemed to genuinely care about ME and my health. Even the young men that meet you at the entrance with a wheelchair and assist you getting to your appointments shared this same concern.  They came to recognize me and were always there with a smile and a wheelchair to help me. I will never forget the day I exited the car while they brought me a wheelchair and told them I didn't need one anymore, I could walk. They all gave me big smiles and a thumbs up at my recovery. It was really a special moment for me.Thanks to my physical therapist and the skills of Dr. Goh my recovery has been very fast. I was able to walk without the need for a walker in just 5 days. My physical therapist didn't like that and urged me to continue to using the walker for an additional week or two. Now, 2 1/2 months later i am walking and climbing stairs at ease. I'm still strengthen the muscles in my legs that had not been used much in the prior 3 years, but I am well on my way to full and complete recovery.I simply cannot express in words my thanks to everyone who attended to me. Customer Service even assisted in getting my Visa extended so I could complete my recovery.  At some point in the future I will surgery on my other need. I have already decided, no matter where in the world I may be when that time comes, I will be returning to Loh Guan Lye and Dr, Goh to have that surgery. I wouldn't even considered having it performed somewhere else.To all of you at Loh Quan Lye, I send you a heartfelt THANK YOU!!! You gave me the rest of my life back!Gene

Review content: Hmmm..I'm a patient who lived in ward for a long period (more than 1 month) , so I think I can voice out for both the patients and healthcare worker part.1. I read through the comments, mostly given less than 3 stars bcoz of altitude problem/ unprofessional / wait for long time in pain.2. From the patients side, I'll say the truth of most of the comments are true. Because I really saw how some staff treat the patients in rude, eg: critic the patients when they are disable,ignore their call of help, some kind of bully.3.From the healthcare worker side, I tried to put in their shoes. I really saw HO(houseman), who are very scare of their boss (MO/Specialist) while duty,I believe that this must be cause by there are bully exist among their workplace. Beside, I saw there are some of the patients, also very rude to them. I also saw one real case who scold the staff nurse very loud in ward before leave.These might be the reasons of why they are lack of regard/cold to patients, bcoz they don't have place to make complaint to for the patients who bully them. And someone say, they are in service line.. others I dunno, but for me, their jobs is treat you healthy, not to serve like babysitter/ maid to you. If you don't appreciate nvm, but dont bully the workers without any reason.4.For the long hours wait issues, I believe that this is not the problem only occur in Malaysia.If you hv read international news, you will notice that even Singapore also have to wait min 3 hours for small cases. Here to educate : In hospital, will have green,yellow,red zone. Green is safe zone, means you still can walk/move/in consious. Red is in harm/ coma, which needs immediately support/treatment. So, there are many thousands of people per day approach to the hospital, in the end, you will still receive the treatment, and dont worry they wont treat you till die, bcoz if they do so, their license will be gantung, then just to be patient and wait.5. For staff don't care patients issue, this I stand neutral. I do believe that many people do not know in GH, you have to take care yourself/ you must have a family members who can take care of you for basic stuff if you are disable, bcos there dont have enough staff. For example, if you can't eat, can't brush ur teeth, how you expect the nurse sit down beside you and just take care of you one person? Do you know some patients if you want them to finish the food..especially elderly/ OKU/Child, it must take very long time. And there are only min4 max 5 staff nurse to handle over 40 patients. If it's really busy I can understand, but I will also saw there have nurse, sitting in their room while duty, patients ask for help bcoz of pain but get scolded...In the end, I hope KKM(Kementerian Kesihatan) can more educate public about the procedure / basic cooperation needed from patients family, how to relief of pain/ basic understanding of some medical terms/ treatments. Many citizens are lack of medical education.Secondly, I do hope healthcare staff, actually you can  change some tone/ words of your speak, I know you doesn't meant that, but if you saw a normal OKU nearby roadside, will you eye-rolling to them/ talk bad words to them? I do believe you won't and nature of human-being are kind. And also, if workers really feel uncomfortable/ bully by people/ feel not worth doing your job bcoz of underpaid, pls voice out.Nowadays  hv social media, you can stand out for your ownself.Lastly,I do hope patients/ consumers, pls stand into others shoes, their workers are help you, they have to face thousands of people per day, millions of people in their life, between these people do anyone really appreciate them from the bottom of heart?   If you received help from other people, you definitely will at least say thank you to them, but I saw many people after cured/ recover n discharged from wad, no much people say thank you to those who save your life..Actually hospital is also a workplace, there are many back side that I can't finished write in this note,overall, hope we can understand each others.

This hospital has a very good coordination between the administration staff and the nurse in the clinic.When we met dr Devindran, my first impression was he is so kind, gentle and very good to make my dad calm. He suggest us to do several examinations like MRI, robotic biopsy and PET scan. Review content: During my Asia travels I have found myself needing medical help three times. Each time I have stayed at Sunway Medical Centre.  I have found the hospital to be modern clean and very well equipped.  The staff, from the reception and counter, to the people who clean the rooms and then the medical staff and doctors and surgeons all are amazingly kind and generous with thier time and care.  Every single person there is truly special. My first visit was for a Colonoscopy and Endoscopy performed by Dr Mohamad Fadli Bin Abd Rahman, a very kind and understanding gentleman is my best description of him.  He put me at ease for what was quite a worrying moment in my life.  A few months later I found myself needing a hernia repair, this time under the care of Dr Heah Hsin Tak.  Once again I found myself in the care of a very fine, skilled and caring doctor who fixed me up.  The lady anaesthetist who looked after me is a very funny lady who put me at ease and made me feel confident I would be taken good care of.  She was so much fun to have around when you feel nervous. Recently I fell down and fractured my collar bone and found myself in the care of Dr Moganadass A/L Muniandy.  His skill at repairing the broken bone with a titanium plate will hopefully outlast me, he is a very kind and skilled doctor and this time the anaesthetist who took care of me was just as brilliant as the first, he did make an impression on my with his care and humour and the way he treated me. Being put to sleep can be worrying, so to have staff that can instantly put you at ease and make you feel safe is very welcome.  The food is quite simply marvelous, nothing like I have experienced  in the UK.  (assuming you are not on a restricted diet during your stay) I am visiting Malaysia on a tourist visa and my last accident was right before my 90 day visa expired so I want to say an even bigger thank you to Lisa, Aina, Alice and Azan at the International Patient Care office.  I had no idea such a thing existed. I turned up there full of worry about how to get a medical extension on my visa so that I have time to recover before moving on.  Within 30 minutes they had completed the paperwork and advised me to go home and wait for a whatsapp message to say a document from kuala lumpur had arrived which I would need for immigration.  Sure enough a few days later they message me, I got to collect the paper work and on to the immigration dept.They took the paperwork from IPC without any questions of me having to fill in any forms. Clearly the IPC know exactly what they are doing!Within 90 minutes I had an extension on my visa so I can recover without the worry of having to travel for a while.  This would not have been possible without the help of IPC so a huge thank you for making the process so easy and worry free. The work you do helping foreign tourists with problems is simply amazing. I highly reccommend Sunway and my top tips if you are staying there is to be prepared, bring your phone charger with a long usb lead, bring your own towels and anything to make your stay a little more comfortable as nothing is provided other than soap and toilet paper in the bathroom of your room.  Bring a couple of towels, a book or two or some headphones for music.  (assuming you have time to plan) Thank You Sunway and everyone who works there.  I hope I never see you again, other than my return visit for a check up on my shoulder in a few weeks time.  But if I do need help in the future, I will be at your door, let's hope from now on I can live hospital free for some time to come.

Review content: Mount Miriam is not just a hospital, going there means that you have joined into a very loving, caring, and supportive family. They go above and beyond for patients and family of patients to feel loved, welcomed, and taken care of.For the first time in my life, I actually felt respected and loved not just as a family of a patient but as a human being. Everyone were so welcoming, so supporting, and so caring.I brought my grandmother here for a late stage cancer. Not much could be done but in Mount Miriam, the staff supported me, my grandmother, my mother, and my family with love, sincerity, and devotion. We prayed together, we hugged and cried together.During radiotherapy, there were volunteers giving free bread for breakfast for everyone. Some also brought carts to provide hot drinks such as milo, coffee, tea, and milk for patients and families of patients.There is a chapel on the 5th floor to pray as well. All religions, backgrounds, ethnicities, faces, color, and race were treated with the utmost love and respect.The place looks old and you can definitely tell that it is a non-profit and a charity based hospital but the people made the place so much better, in my opinion, then more expensive hospitals such as Island Hospital. But don't let the old building fool you, they have cutting edge equipment, excellent services, and world class doctors, nurses, and staff.There was even this one time where I came in late after their office has closed to pick up a medication for my grandmother (my fault) and the cashier still waited for me and the pharmacist drove from her house to the hospital to get my grandmother her medication. I have never encountered that in any hospital.Special mentions to Dr Choong for taking good care of my grandmother and my family. Thank you for answering our questions patiently, clearly, and lovingly. Thank you for respecting and caring for my grandmother. You have done your best and I appreciate all you have done.Thank you to Jane for always supporting us, tending to our every need, questions, inquiries. For sorting out all the medication and schedules for us. For being so kind, understanding, and loving to us.Thank you to Emily from the pastoral who guided us with prayer and for being there to give us support when we were so lost and confused.Thank you to Peter for meeting us on that Wednesday when my grandmother had radio therapy. Your laughter and kindess was so contagious! You bring joy to the people around you and thank you for the milo! Through your volunteering, you bring hope and light into the darkness.Thank you to Ibu Salbiah who essentially became my second mother. Always remembers my name, my wife's, my mother's, my grandmother's. For always giving us strength, love, affection, care, and prayers. You have accepted us into the family of Mount Miriam and that is something we will hold on to for the rest of our lives. My grandmother (Ibu Dian) will always remember you and the love you have showed us. I hope to meet you again soon.Last but not least, thank you to the entire staff and management who have made and kept the place running. You have given HOPE and LOVE to people with cancer and their families. I pray for you and I will always remember you all.I hope one day I have the opportunity to give back to Mount Miriam. Thank you. I love you all.

Review content: Hospital known for osteopathic and cancer treatments in addition to a wide variety of other medical services.  Cash, credit card and probably e-wallet payments accepted.Not as glitzy or streamlined as a Bangkok hospital, Gleneagles nonetheless caters not just to locals but also an international clientele.  Request appointments in advance online.  When you arrive, register at the International Patients office on the ground floor.  They'll check your passport and obtain other basic contact information before referring you to the floor and office of your appointment.At this point things break down a bit.  Signage is reasonably good to help you find where you're going, but at times it's missing and you have to wander a bit.  You know you're in the right general area, but you may need to round a corner into another lobby area to find your particular office number.There are no instructions on what to do when you arrive.  Apparently you just sit down and wait for your name to be called.  But this isn't clearly stated anywhere so be prepared to be patient as well as find a staff member to inquire of.  Staff are generally friendly.Appointments are efficient, depending on the nature of your medical issue.  Blood tests and x-rays can be done in-house and in a remarkably quick fashion.   Prices are good by Western standards but probably high by Malaysian standards.  Self-pay is the default, but you can try showing your proof of insurance if you want.  For a doctor consult, blood work and x-rays and then a secondary consult for the physician to examine the aforementioned test results and pronounce a prognosis and prescribe any medications applicable, the cost was just under 800 MYR.  Total time (including an hour for lunch) was under four hours.Seems like a decent enough place just be prepared for some minor confusion.

Review content: We traveled from Indonesia to Penang to seek treatment for my mom's osteoarthritis on her knees. From the beginning, it was easy to contact and communicate the hospital. I opened PAH web and talked to the staff via WhatsApp. Then I was instructed to download the app, in which I booked an appointment with an orthopedist. All very easy and straightforward.On the D-day, we met with Dr Ho Shu Chien. He promptly assessed my mom's knees, explained to us her condition, and offered 2 solutions, temporary and long-term (which Indonesian doctors didn't do). He showed us videos of a patient who underwent total knee replacement surgery. But since my mom didn't dare to have surgery, she opted for the temporary solution, which is an injection to her knees. Dr Chien then told us there are 3 options of medicine, the lower grade, the medium grade, and the highest grade. He also informed the price of each option. We opted for the highest grade, and the procedure was done on the same day. We had to wait for about an hour, then the procedure was carried out.After that, the administrative process was swift and prompt. The whole payment and handover of outpatient meds were done in less than 20 mins. I am most impressed by the bills. The bills detailed every single little thing used for my mom's procedure, down to the band-aids used on her knees after the injection, along with the price. We were surprised to see Dr Chien gave a 25% discount of his procedure fees and also waived the anesthesia used on her knees. We are very thankful of him!We thank the Penang Adventist Hospital for taking such a good care of my mom. Would definitely recommend to friends & family, and hope will be able to come back in the future should there be more ailments.
